page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-lc1m4.large is a shared, burstable virtual instance designed for low-utilization tasks with occasional compute bursts. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration exposes 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via hyperthreading, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include vector instruction extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside cryptographic AES acceleration.

The instance does not include integrated local storage and operates with a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses assigned. Hardware accelerator support is absent, with 0 GPUs provisioned. The hypervisor layer is managed via KVM.

Benchmark outcomes reflect its burstable, shared-core profile, placing the instance primarily in lower performance tiers under sustained stress. In computational testing, the server recorded a single-core stress-ng score of 1093.49 and a multi-core score of 2133.08. Geekbench scores reached 880.0 for single-core and 1470.0 for multi-core evaluations. Memory bandwidth measurements show 16.1 GB/sec for large block reads and 13.81 GB/sec for large block writes. Under application testing, static web serving delivered 2.22 GB/sec throughput, while Redis processed 1.47 million SET operations per second.

Given its burstable CPU allocation and lack of dedicated compute cores, sustained execution will face CPU throttling once credits are exhausted. It provides a cost-efficient resource density for memory-oriented tasks that do not demand sustained CPU throughput. Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-lc1m4.large is appropriate for lightweight web serving, development environments, staging systems, and intermittent background batch or automation jobs.
